Embedding Paired Free-Fermion Gaussian States into Gutzwiller-Projected Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer Wave Functions

Ryui Kaneko ††thanks: E-mail address: ryuikaneko@sophia.ac.jp
Abstract

Gutzwiller-projected Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) wave functions of Abrikosov fermions are widely used to describe quantum many-body states. Taking the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model as an example, we exactly embed any even-parity spinless fermionic Gaussian state representable as a paired exponential in the chosen particle basis into a projected BCS state of spinful Abrikosov fermions. The construction provides controlled initial states for variational Monte Carlo studies of nonintegrable models.

Variational wave functions provide concrete representations of quantum phases. Gutzwiller-projected Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) states describe a wide range of strongly correlated phases [2, 5, 9] and, in special cases, become exact ground states of quantum spin models [6, 17, 1, 11, 21, 8, 12]. Nevertheless, an explicit Abrikosov-fermion projected-BCS representation has not been established even for the well-known one-dimensional (1D) transverse-field Ising (TFI) model, although its ground state is exactly solvable as a Gaussian state of Jordan–Wigner (JW) fermions [14]. Here we provide such a construction by introducing an auxiliary Pfaffian that evaluates to unity for every spin configuration.

We consider the 1D TFI model on a periodic chain of even LL sites:

HTFI=−J∑j=1Lσjxσj+1x−h∑j=1Lσjz,g=h/J,J>0,\displaystyle H_{\mathrm{TFI}}=-J\sum_{j=1}^{L}\sigma_{j}^{x}\sigma_{j+1}^{x}-h\sum_{j=1}^{L}\sigma_{j}^{z},\quad g=h/J,\quad J>0, (1)

where JJ is the coupling constant and hh is the strength of the transverse field. The operators σjx\sigma_{j}^{x} and σjz\sigma_{j}^{z} are Pauli matrices. After the JW transformation defined by σjz=1−2​aj†​aj=1−2​nj\sigma_{j}^{z}=1-2a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{j}=1-2n_{j} and σjx=[∏ℓ<j(1−2​nℓ)]​(aj†+aj)\sigma_{j}^{x}=\left[\prod_{\ell<j}(1-2n_{\ell})\right](a_{j}^{\dagger}+a_{j}), spins are replaced by noninteracting fermions under antiperiodic boundary conditions for the finite-system even-parity ground state. Identifying a down spin with an occupied site, the ground state, up to an overall normalization, is given by

|ΨJW⟩\displaystyle|\Psi_{\mathrm{JW}}\rangle =exp(∑i,j=1Lψi,j2ai†aj†)|0⟩,ψi,j=1L∑kei​k​(j−i)ψk,\displaystyle=\exp\!\left(\sum_{i,j=1}^{L}\frac{\psi_{i,j}}{2}a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j}^{\dagger}\right)\lvert 0\rangle,\quad\psi_{i,j}=\frac{1}{L}\sum_{k}e^{\mathrm{i}k(j-i)}\psi_{k}, (2)
ψk\displaystyle\psi_{k} =i​sin⁡kg−cos⁡k+ϵk,ϵk=1+g2−2​g​cos⁡k,\displaystyle=\mathrm{i}\frac{\sin k}{g-\cos k+\epsilon_{k}},\quad\epsilon_{k}=\sqrt{1+g^{2}-2g\cos k}, (3)

with the momenta defined by k=2​π​(m+1/2)/Lk=2\pi(m+1/2)/L for m=0,1,…,L−1m=0,1,\ldots,L-1. For a given |D⟩=ad1†ad2†⋯ad2​m†|0⟩|D\rangle=a_{d_{1}}^{\dagger}a_{d_{2}}^{\dagger}\cdots a_{d_{2m}}^{\dagger}\lvert 0\rangle, with the set of down-spin sites D={d1,d2,…,d2​m}D=\{d_{1},d_{2},\dots,d_{2m}\} (d1<d2<⋯<d2​md_{1}<d_{2}<\cdots<d_{2m}), the overlap between |D⟩|D\rangle and the ground state is

ΨJW​(D)=12m​m!​∑τ∈𝔖2​msgn⁡(τ)​∏j=1mψdτ⁡(2​j−1),dτ⁡(2​j)=Pf⁡𝝍D,\displaystyle\Psi_{\mathrm{JW}}(D)=\frac{1}{2^{m}m!}\sum_{\tau\in\mathfrak{S}_{2m}}\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\prod_{j=1}^{m}\psi_{d_{\tau(2j-1)},d_{\tau(2j)}}=\operatorname{Pf}\bm{\psi}_{D}, (4)

where 𝝍D\bm{\psi}_{D} is a 2​m×2​m2m\times 2m antisymmetric matrix with elements ψda,db\psi_{d_{a},d_{b}} for a,b=1,2,…,2​ma,b=1,2,\dots,2m, 𝔖2​m\mathfrak{S}_{2m} is the set of all permutations of 1,2,…,2​m1,2,\dots,2m, and Pf\operatorname{Pf} represents a Pfaffian.

This wave function ΨJW​(D)\Psi_{\mathrm{JW}}(D) can be embedded into the projected BCS representation of Abrikosov fermions, satisfying |↑⟩j=cj,↑†|0⟩|\uparrow\rangle_{j}=c_{j,\uparrow}^{\dagger}\lvert 0\rangle and |↓⟩j=cj,↓†|0⟩|\downarrow\rangle_{j}=c_{j,\downarrow}^{\dagger}\lvert 0\rangle, with nj,↑+nj,↓=1n_{j,\uparrow}+n_{j,\downarrow}=1. Let us define the wave function

|Φ[F]⟩=PGexp(∑i,j=1L∑α,β∈{↑,↓}Fi,jα,β2ci,α†cj,β†)|0⟩,\displaystyle|\Phi[F]\rangle=P_{\mathrm{G}}\exp\!\left(\sum_{i,j=1}^{L}\sum_{\alpha,\beta\in\{\uparrow,\downarrow\}}\frac{F_{i,j}^{\alpha,\beta}}{2}c_{i,\alpha}^{\dagger}c_{j,\beta}^{\dagger}\right)\lvert 0\rangle, (5)

where Fi,jα,β=−Fj,iβ,αF_{i,j}^{\alpha,\beta}=-F_{j,i}^{\beta,\alpha} is a pairing amplitude and PG=∏iδni,↑+ni,↓,1P_{\mathrm{G}}=\prod_{i}\delta_{n_{i,\uparrow}+n_{i,\downarrow},1} imposes one fermion per site. We choose

Fi,j↓,↓=ψi,j,Fi,j↑,↑=si,j,Fi,j↑,↓=−Fj,i↓,↑=0,\displaystyle F_{i,j}^{\downarrow,\downarrow}=\psi_{i,j},\quad F_{i,j}^{\uparrow,\uparrow}=s_{i,j},\quad F_{i,j}^{\uparrow,\downarrow}=-F_{j,i}^{\downarrow,\uparrow}=0, (6)

with si,j=−sgn⁡(i−j)=1,−1,0s_{i,j}=-\operatorname{sgn}(i-j)=1,-1,0 for i<ji<j, i>ji>j, and i=ji=j, respectively. Let U={u1,u2,…,u2​p}U=\{u_{1},u_{2},\dots,u_{2p}\} (u1<u2<⋯<u2​pu_{1}<u_{2}<\cdots<u_{2p}, 2​p=L−2​m2p=L-2m) be the up-spin set, complementary to the down-spin set DD. We define the fermionic representative of each physical spin configuration by

|x⟩=cu1,↑†⋯cu2​p,↑†cd1,↓†⋯cd2​m,↓†|0⟩.\displaystyle|x\rangle=c_{u_{1},\uparrow}^{\dagger}\cdots c_{u_{2p},\uparrow}^{\dagger}c_{d_{1},\downarrow}^{\dagger}\cdots c_{d_{2m},\downarrow}^{\dagger}|0\rangle. (7)

Here, all up-spin operators precede the down-spin operators, with each set ordered by increasing site index. Equation (7) defines the spin-to-fermion basis mapping, rather than a reordering of a separately defined site-ordered Fock basis. A different ordering transforms both the basis states and the pairing matrix consistently, leaving the physical spin state unchanged. Because |x⟩|x\rangle already contains exactly one fermion per site, ⟨x|​PG=⟨x|\langle x|P_{\mathrm{G}}=\langle x| holds. Hence,

Φ⁡(x)\displaystyle\Phi(x) =⟨x|Φ[F]⟩=⟨0|cd2​m,↓⋯cd1,↓cu2​p,↑⋯cu1,↑\displaystyle=\langle x|\Phi[F]\rangle=\langle 0|c_{d_{2m},\downarrow}\cdots c_{d_{1},\downarrow}c_{u_{2p},\uparrow}\cdots c_{u_{1},\uparrow}
×exp⁡[∑i,j=1Lsi,j2​ci,↑†​cj,↑†+∑i,j=1Lψi,j2​ci,↓†​cj,↓†]​|0⟩.\displaystyle\times\exp\left[\sum_{i,j=1}^{L}\frac{s_{i,j}}{2}c_{i,\uparrow}^{\dagger}c_{j,\uparrow}^{\dagger}+\sum_{i,j=1}^{L}\frac{\psi_{i,j}}{2}c_{i,\downarrow}^{\dagger}c_{j,\downarrow}^{\dagger}\right]|0\rangle. (8)

Only the term containing pp up-spin pairs and mm down-spin pairs contributes to the amplitude, and the corresponding principal submatrix of the pairing matrix is block diagonal:

𝑭x=(𝒔U00𝝍D),(𝒔U)a,b=sua,ub,(𝝍D)a,b=ψda,db.\displaystyle\bm{F}_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}\bm{s}_{U}&0\\ 0&\bm{\psi}_{D}\end{pmatrix},\quad(\bm{s}_{U})_{a,b}=s_{u_{a},u_{b}},\quad(\bm{\psi}_{D})_{a,b}=\psi_{d_{a},d_{b}}. (9)

Since the Pfaffian of a block diagonal matrix is the product of the Pfaffians of its blocks, Φ⁡(x)=Pf⁡𝑭x=Pf⁡𝒔U⋅Pf⁡𝝍D\Phi(x)=\operatorname{Pf}\bm{F}_{x}=\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{U}\cdot\operatorname{Pf}\bm{\psi}_{D} holds. No additional permutation sign appears because the operator ordering in Eq. (7) matches the block ordering in 𝑭x\bm{F}_{x}.

Since u1<⋯<u2​pu_{1}<\cdots<u_{2p}, the restricted antisymmetric matrix 𝒔U\bm{s}_{U} has matrix elements (𝒔U)a,b=1(\bm{s}_{U})_{a,b}=1 for a<ba<b and (𝒔U)a,b=−1(\bm{s}_{U})_{a,b}=-1 for a>ba>b, independently of the actual sites contained in UU. Then, denoting this 2​p×2​p2p\times 2p matrix 𝒔U\bm{s}_{U} by 𝒔2​p\bm{s}_{2p} and expanding its Pfaffian along the first row gives Pf⁡𝒔2​p=∑j=22​p(−1)j​Pf⁡𝒔2​p−2=(1−1+⋯+1−1+1)​Pf⁡𝒔2​p−2=Pf⁡𝒔2​p−2\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{2p}=\sum_{j=2}^{2p}(-1)^{j}\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{2p-2}=(1-1+\cdots+1-1+1)\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{2p-2}=\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{2p-2}. Together with Pf⁡𝒔2=1\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{2}=1 and the convention Pf⁡𝒔0=1\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{0}=1, this equation proves Pf⁡𝒔U=1\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{U}=1 for every up-spin configuration complementary to DD. Therefore,

Φ⁡(x)=Pf⁡𝒔U⋅Pf⁡𝝍D=1⋅Pf⁡𝝍D=ΨJW​(D)\displaystyle\Phi(x)=\operatorname{Pf}\bm{s}_{U}\cdot\operatorname{Pf}\bm{\psi}_{D}=1\cdot\operatorname{Pf}\bm{\psi}_{D}=\Psi_{\mathrm{JW}}(D) (10)

holds for any even-sized down-spin configuration DD. Note that, for an odd number of down spins, both amplitudes vanish because both states contain only fermion pairs. Since the proof uses only the Pfaffian form in Eq. (4), the construction applies to any pure even-parity spinless fermionic Gaussian state on an even number of sites that has a nonzero overlap with the particle vacuum and admits the paired exponential representation of Eq. (2) in the chosen particle basis.

The pairing matrices Fi,j↑,↑F_{i,j}^{\uparrow,\uparrow} and Fi,j↓,↓F_{i,j}^{\downarrow,\downarrow} in Eq. (6) are long-ranged in real space, but both can be obtained from local parent Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonians on a finite-size antiperiodic momentum grid. The physical block can be obtained by a nearest-neighbor spinless pp-wave model with the hopping amplitude tαt_{\alpha}, the chemical potential μα\mu_{\alpha}, and the pairing amplitude Δα\Delta_{\alpha}, specified by

ξkα=−2​tα​cos⁡k−μα,Δkα=2​i​Δα​sin⁡k,\displaystyle\xi_{k}^{\alpha}=-2t_{\alpha}\cos k-\mu_{\alpha},\quad\Delta_{k}^{\alpha}=2\mathrm{i}\Delta_{\alpha}\sin k, (11)

through Fkα=Δkα/[Ekα+ξkα]F_{k}^{\alpha}=\Delta_{k}^{\alpha}/[E_{k}^{\alpha}+\xi_{k}^{\alpha}] with Ekα=(ξkα)2+|Δkα|2E_{k}^{\alpha}=\sqrt{(\xi_{k}^{\alpha})^{2}+|\Delta_{k}^{\alpha}|^{2}} (α=↑,↓\alpha=\uparrow,\downarrow). For the spin-down component, we can choose t↓=Δ↓=J/2t_{\downarrow}=\Delta_{\downarrow}=J/2 and μ↓=−J​g\mu_{\downarrow}=-Jg, which gives the dispersion Ek↓=J​ϵkE_{k}^{\downarrow}=J\epsilon_{k} of the 1D TFI model. For the spin-up component, we can choose t↑=−Δ↑=J/2t_{\uparrow}=-\Delta_{\uparrow}=J/2 and μ↑=0\mu_{\uparrow}=0, which results in a flat-band nearest-neighbor Kitaev chain with Ek↑=JE_{k}^{\uparrow}=J and Fk↑=sk=−i​cot⁡(k/2)F_{k}^{\uparrow}=s_{k}=-\mathrm{i}\cot(k/2). Since e−i​k​L=−1e^{-\mathrm{i}kL}=-1 for the antiperiodic momenta and hence ∑r=1L−1e−i​k​r=−i​cot⁡(k/2)\sum_{r=1}^{L-1}e^{-\mathrm{i}kr}=-\mathrm{i}\cot(k/2), the inverse discrete Fourier transform gives Fi,j↑,↑=si,j=−sgn⁡(i−j)F^{\uparrow,\uparrow}_{i,j}=s_{i,j}=-\operatorname{sgn}(i-j) with the antiperiodic continuation si,j+L=−si,js_{i,j+L}=-s_{i,j}.

The present construction also applies to even-length spin-1/21/2 chains with JW ground states of the paired Gaussian form in Eq. (2), beyond the TFI model. Examples include appropriate even-parity ground-state sectors of the anisotropic XY chain [10, 3] and cluster-Ising chains [18, 19]. For the latter class, the construction embeds the ground states described by Eq. (2), including representatives of the Ising-ordered and cluster-symmetry-protected-topological (SPT) regimes [4, 15]. Therefore, it places the corresponding ordered, critical, and SPT states within a common projected-BCS manifold.

The exact state can also serve as a controlled variational initial state away from integrability. For example, adding a longitudinal field yields H=HTFI−hx​∑jσjxH=H_{\mathrm{TFI}}-h_{x}\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}^{x}, whose JW representation is no longer quadratic when hx≠0h_{x}\neq 0. On the other hand, for hx≫J,hh_{x}\gg J,h, the ground state approaches ∏j(cj,↑†+cj,↓†)|0⟩\prod_{j}(c_{j,\uparrow}^{\dagger}+c_{j,\downarrow}^{\dagger})\lvert 0\rangle up to normalization. In general, a product state ∏j(u​cj,↑†+v​cj,↓†)​|0⟩\prod_{j}(uc_{j,\uparrow}^{\dagger}+vc_{j,\downarrow}^{\dagger})|0\rangle is obtained by choosing Fi,jα,β=si,j​wα​wβF_{i,j}^{\alpha,\beta}=s_{i,j}w_{\alpha}w_{\beta}, where w↑=uw_{\uparrow}=u and w↓=vw_{\downarrow}=v. Therefore, we naturally expect the projected BCS state to provide a good variational ansatz for finite hxh_{x}. To examine this expectation, we perform variational Monte Carlo (VMC) calculations. We fix the parameters J=h=1J=h=1 and vary the longitudinal field from hx=0h_{x}=0 to hx=2h_{x}=2 at L=64L=64. The pairing amplitudes Fi,jα,βF_{i,j}^{\alpha,\beta} are assumed to be translationally invariant up to an overall sign and are optimized starting from the hx=0h_{x}=0 state specified by Fi,jα,αF_{i,j}^{\alpha,\alpha}, together with small initial random values of Fi,j↑,↓=−Fj,i↓,↑F_{i,j}^{\uparrow,\downarrow}=-F_{j,i}^{\downarrow,\uparrow}. As shown in Fig. 1, the optimized VMC energy agrees with the nearly exact DMRG energy within the statistical errors. The total energy variance of the optimized VMC state is less than 3×10−53\times 10^{-5} for 0≤hx≤20\leq h_{x}\leq 2.

In summary, using the exact solution of the 1D TFI model as an example, we have presented a method for embedding an even-parity spinless Gaussian state that admits a paired exponential representation on an even lattice into an Abrikosov-fermion projected BCS state. In this embedding, the auxiliary up-spin Pfaffian is unity for any choice of up-spin sites, yielding an exact projected BCS representation of the Gaussian state in the physical spin Hilbert space. Our result supplies a natural starting point for variational studies of ground states in nonintegrable quantum systems. Extensions to odd-parity states, multiband Gaussian states, and higher-dimensional fermionization with nontrivial gauge sectors remain open.
